premise, label, and hypothesis of an NLI instance

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple similar task descriptions into a single normalized form. Added RoBERTa-large which was missing from extracted models. Removed redundant/extraneous descriptions of outputs.

automatic_metrics: confidence score from an NLI model

changes_made.explanation: Removed all metrics as they are not used to evaluate NLG quality directly. The paper uses confidence scores and z-statistics for data selection/filtering, label consistency during training, but doesn't use standard NLG evaluation metrics like BLEU/ROUGE to evaluate the generated text quality.
Cleaned up empty/null values. Paper does not use LLMs as judges for evaluating generated outputs.
Cleaned up empty/null values. Paper does not conduct human evaluation of the generated outputs.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on generating debiased NLG datasets for NLI, but primarily evaluates the utility of these generated datasets by training NLI classifiers and testing them on various benchmarks. While they generated natural language data, they didn't evaluate the generation quality using standard NLG metrics or human evaluation. Instead, they evaluated downstream task performance (NLI classification accuracy).
